newsitem.title: EGYPT: Doctors find fetus in Egyptian boy's stomach.
newsitem.headline: Doctors find fetus in Egyptian boy's stomach.

text.p: An Egyptian teenager who complained of stomach pains was found to have his underdeveloped twin fetus lodged above his abdomen where it had been slowly feeding off him for the past 16 years, medical sources said on Wednesday.
They said doctors found an 18-cm long fetus weighing two kg (4.4 lbs) with a head, an arm, a tongue and fully-formed teeth when they operated on Hisham Ragab, 16, a building worker.
An X-ray had shown a swollen sac had been pressing against his kidneys.

Medical examination of the teeth found in the fetal mouth cavity revealed that they were those of a 16-year-old, indicating that the fetus had been feeding off Ragab's cells for survival, medical sources said.

Doctors said the incident occurred because the fertilised ovum did not divide into two as it usually does in the case of twins. Instead of splitting apart, Ragab's underdeveloped twin had grown inside the originally fertilised ovum.
Occurences of incomplete ovum division are not uncommon, but it was the first time that doctors in Egypt had found such a resulting mature fetus, medical sources said.
Hospital officials said Ragab was in good health and he would be released from hospital once he recovers from surgery.
